Without their parents and Kweiya’s knowledge, this had made Niko and Kiara grow envious.

One day, Mother Baria fell ill. Father Bone had to stay home to take care of her and to harvest their farm. He asked his children to find red fruits to cure Mother Baria on the edges of the forest. Kweiya, Niko, and Kiara went to the forest. However, Niko and Kiara were secretly planning something. They persuaded Kweiya to go further into the forest. Kweiya was doubtful about their safety in the unknown part of the forest, but Niko and Kiara convinced him by spinning a story that the deepest part of the forest had more red fruits than other places in the forest. At first, the three of them went in together. Kweiya looked around in amazement at the beautiful scenery that he had never seen before. But then, Niko and Kiara left him when Kweiya was too engrossed in picking the red fruits.

Later, Kweiya felt that he had gotten enough red fruits and was about to go home, but the night had fallen. He couldn’t see the way back out of the forest. He was lost. Meanwhile back at home, his two siblings had returned and told their parents that Kweiya insisted on going into the deepest part of the forest. When Mother’s health finally recovered, she heard a trill of birdsong. Outside, there was a handsome bird with colorful feathers. It dropped red fruits to the ground. It sang again to her one last time and then flew away, never to be seen again.

Ingredients:

  • 2 eggs
  • 2 teaspoons butter or olive oil
  • 1 small potato, diced
  • 2-3 tablespoons onion, finely crushed
  • 3 cloves garlic, finely crushed
  • 3-4 cherry tomatoes, roughly chopped
  • Salt and pepper, to taste
  • 2 handfuls of baby spinach, wash and drain

Preparations and Cooking:

  1. First, prepare all of your vegetables and spices. Prepare the egg too by cracking them into a bowl.
  2. Next, heat the oil or butter in a pan over medium-high heat until it’s sizzling.
  3. Then, put the potato in and increase the heat a little. Stir-fry the potato around three to five minutes. Check the tenderness; the potato is ready when you can easily stick it with a fork.
  4. After that, add the onion into the stir-fry. Stir again for another two minutes or until the onion becomes a bit brown. Add in the garlic and stir for a further minute. Then add the tomato and stir-fry about one more minute.
  5. When the stir-fry’s juice cooks off, finally take the stir-fry pan off the heat. Immediately add the eggs to the pan, then stir. As you mix, the remaining heat will quite cook the egg. Add salt and pepper to taste. If the egg is not fully cooked, put the pan back on very low heat, stir frequently, and slowly cook the scramble well done. This method keeps the egg tender and creamy.
  6. To finish, toss the spinach into the pan and stir until it wilts. You can also add it just before serving so that the spinach stays raw.
  7. Serve the vegetable scramble on top of toast, on top of rice, or with a salad of your choice.

She also connected us with trainers who would observe and assist the internship participants when we encountered obstacles or did not understand the material on the MageHub platform.

We did all of these activities online.

The training coordinator would assign a case study project to the students after completing the training class. The theme and level of difficulty of the project would be determined based on the participants' evaluation and work results in the training class. I felt nervous and excited when our trainers commented on our tasks. The trainers’ comments greatly helped me develop the assigned case study project.

Elsa, a grade 11 culinary student from Yogyakarta, had always loved baking. Her cookies were popular among friends and family, but she never thought of selling them—until her teacher assigned a project on small business development.

Elsa decided to give it a try. She baked a batch of chocolate chip cookies and posted a few photos on her Instagram account with the caption, “Homemade and fresh! DM to order.” She didn’t expect much, but within a few hours, she had five orders.

That weekend, she baked more cookies and started packaging them in simple boxes with hand-written thank-you notes. She called her brand Elsa’s Sweet Bites. Every evening after school, she baked and packed cookies, sometimes with help from her younger sister.

The orders kept coming. Her friends shared her posts, and even some teachers placed orders. Elsa learned how to calculate prices, manage time, and talk to customers. That moment taught her the importance of honesty and effective communication in business.

After three months, she had saved enough money to buy a new hand mixer. “It’s not just a project anymore,” she told her teacher. “It’s my business.”

Her teacher smiled. “That’s what entrepreneurship is all about. Starting small and growing with heart.”
